common.disclaimer: Wellness is not a medical device. Recommendations follow general WHO guidelines and do not replace a doctor’s advice.

onboarding.welcomeText: A free, open-source health tracker. All your data stays on your phone. Answer a few questions and the app will calculate your personal targets.
onboarding.name: What should we call you (optional)

healthyRange.$t: Healthy weight for your height: {0:n0}–{1:n0} kg (BMI 18.5–24.9).

onboarding.bmiHintTitle: What BMI is and how far to trust it
onboarding.bmiHint: Body mass index = weight / height². It is a rough guide: it overstates “fatness” in muscular athletes and may understate it in older people. Body fat percentage and waist size are better — track them in the Body section.
onboarding.activityText: How active is your normal day, NOT counting workouts? Workouts and steps above 3,000 are counted separately.
onboarding.bmrHint: Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is the energy your body uses at complete rest (Mifflin–St Jeor equation), multiplied by an activity factor. If you know your BMR precisely (e.g. from bioimpedance), you can set it in settings.
onboarding.finishText: Choose what you want to track. You can change it later in settings.
onboarding.normNote: On workout days the target increases automatically.

pace.title: Weight change pace

eta.$t: You should reach your goal in about {0:n0} weeks.

pace.mismatch: The pace points away from your goal weight.

warnings.lossFast: More than 1 % of body weight per week — high risk of muscle loss and relapse.
warnings.lossVeryFast: Very fast loss: risk of muscle loss, gallstones and nutrient deficiencies. Not recommended without medical supervision.
warnings.gainFast: Gaining faster than 0.5 kg/week is mostly fat.

pace.hint: Safe weight loss is 0.5–1 % of body weight per week. Slower makes results easier to keep and preserves muscle. For muscle gain, 0.25–0.5 kg per week is optimal. The slider’s centre means maintaining your current weight.

lifestyles.label: Sedentary
lifestyles.hint: Desk job or study, little walking (under 4k steps)

lifestyles.label: Light
lifestyles.hint: Desk job, but I walk a lot for errands

lifestyles.label: Moderate
lifestyles.hint: On my feet at work: shop assistant, teacher, waiter

kcal.label: Calories
kcal.rec: Spread calories over 3–4 meals. Build meals around vegetables, protein and whole grains; the emptiest calories are sugary drinks, pastries and fast food.
kcal.hint: Energy from food. Below the minimum your body starts breaking down muscle and saving energy. Above the maximum your weight goal is out of reach.

protein.label: Protein
protein.rec: Include a protein source in every meal: 20–40 g at a time (eggs, cottage cheese, chicken, fish, legumes, Greek yogurt).
protein.hint: Building material for muscles, enzymes and immunity. 0.8 g/kg is the minimum, 1.4–1.6 g/kg is optimal with training or weight loss. At high body weight it is based on an adjusted weight.

fat.label: Fat
fat.rec: Rely on vegetable oils, nuts and fish. Limit fried food and fatty meat; avoid trans fats.
fat.hint: Needed for hormones and absorbing vitamins A, D, E, K. Aim for 20–35 % of calories, preferably from fish, nuts and vegetable oils.

carbs.label: Carbs
carbs.rec: Choose slow carbs: grains, wholegrain bread, legumes, vegetables and fruit instead of sweets and white bread.
carbs.hint: Main fuel for the brain and muscles. 130 g is the brain’s glucose need. Prefer grains, vegetables, fruit and legumes.

sugar.label: Sugars (total)
sugar.rec: Fruit and dairy are fine sources of sugar. Watch added sugar first.
sugar.hint: All sugars, including natural ones from fruit and milk. Sugars inside whole foods are less harmful than added sugars.

addedSugar.label: Added sugar
addedSugar.rec: Swap sugary drinks for water or unsweetened tea, choose plain yogurt and porridge, read ingredient lists.
addedSugar.hint: Sugar, honey, syrups, juices. WHO: under 10 % of calories, ideally under 5 %. A main driver of tooth decay, obesity and type 2 diabetes.

sodium.label: Sodium
sodium.rec: Eat fewer sausages, cheeses, sauces and ready meals; salt at the end of cooking; use spices and lemon instead.
sodium.hint: Mostly from salt (1 g salt ≈ 400 mg sodium). WHO: no more than 2000 mg (5 g salt). Excess raises blood pressure.

fiber.label: Fiber
fiber.rec: Vegetables with every meal, wholegrain bread, buckwheat, oats, legumes, berries, flaxseed.
fiber.hint: Feeds gut bacteria, keeps you full, lowers cholesterol and colon cancer risk. Aim for 25–35 g a day.

satFat.label: Saturated fat
satFat.rec: Replace some butter and fatty meat with fish, poultry, vegetable oils and nuts.
satFat.hint: Fatty meat, butter, cheese, palm oil. Under 10 % of calories lowers heart disease risk.

transFat.label: Trans fat
transFat.rec: Avoid margarine, deep-fried food and cheap pastries; look for “partially hydrogenated” on labels.
transFat.hint: Margarine, deep-fried food, cheap pastries. There is no safe dose — the less the better. WHO: under 1 % of calories.

cholesterol.label: Cholesterol
cholesterol.rec: Main sources are eggs, offal and fatty meat. Limiting saturated and trans fats matters more.
cholesterol.hint: Dietary cholesterol affects blood levels less than saturated and trans fats, but with heart disease risk keep it under 300 mg.

potassium.label: Potassium
potassium.rec: Potatoes, bananas, beans, dried apricots, spinach, avocado and kefir are good sources.
potassium.hint: Counterbalances sodium: lowers blood pressure, supports heart and muscles. WHO: at least 3500 mg. Vegetables, fruit, legumes, potatoes.

advice.kcalOver: Calories are above the maximum. A one-off is fine — enable adaptive targets in settings and the app will spread the surplus over the week.
advice.kcalUnder: Too few calories. A large deficit slows your metabolism and burns muscle. Add a proper meal.
advice.proteinUnder: Low on protein. Try cottage cheese, eggs, chicken, fish, legumes or Greek yogurt.
advice.proteinOver: Protein is well above target. Usually not harmful for healthy kidneys, but it crowds out vegetables and grains.
advice.addedSugarOver: Added sugar is above the WHO limit. The main sources are sugary drinks, juices, pastries and sweetened yogurts.
advice.sodiumOver: More than 5 g of salt. Sausages, cheese, sauces, bread and ready meals hide a lot of it. Balance with potassium: vegetables, fruit, legumes.
advice.satFatOver: Saturated fat is above 10 % of calories. Swap some butter and fatty meat for fish, nuts and vegetable oils.
advice.transFatOver: Trans fats are above the limit. Check pastries, fast food and margarine.
advice.fiberUnder: Low on fiber. Add vegetables, wholegrain bread, buckwheat, oats, legumes and berries.
advice.potassiumUnder: Low on potassium. Potatoes, bananas, beans, dried apricots, spinach and kefir are good sources.
advice.cholesterolOver: Cholesterol is above 300 mg. This matters if your blood cholesterol is high or you have heart disease.
advice.fatUnder: Very little fat — this hurts hormones and vitamin absorption. Add nuts, fish or oil in your salad.
advice.allGoodLate: Great day: everything is within the recommended ranges!
advice.allGoodSoFar: All good so far. Keep it up!

summary.weekHint: Green bars are a deficit (you burned more than you ate), orange bars a surplus. Grey means no food logged that day. About 7700 kcal equal 1 kg of body fat.

nutrition.scalesHint: Yellow is below the safe minimum, green is the recommended range, red is above the maximum. The vertical line is your target. “Limits” (sugar, salt, trans fat, cholesterol) have no lower bound. Nutrients missing from a product count as 0.
nutrition.bandNote: Green band is the recommended range, dashed line the target.
nutrition.emptyLog: Nothing logged for this day. Tap “Add food”.

sheet.noFoods: None of today’s entries contain this nutrient

edit.name: Name
edit.hint: Check the nutrition table on the package. Sodium (mg) = salt (g) × 400. Empty fields count as 0. For a home-made dish, add up the ingredients and divide by the final weight × 100.
edit.saltNote: Salt on the label? E.g. 1.2 g salt = 480 mg sodium.

status.ok: In range, but not at the goal yet
status.high: Above your usual norm — don’t overdo it

water.otherHint: Tea, coffee, juice, milk, soup… Counted for the danger limit but not towards your plain-water target.

dangerNote.$t: The danger limit counts all fluid you drank (now {0:n2} L).

hint: The target is about 33 ml per kg of body weight plus ~500 ml per hour of exercise that day. At high body weight it uses an adjusted weight — fat tissue needs very little water.
About 20 % of water comes from food; that is already accounted for.
Danger zone: kidneys can excrete ~1 L per hour. Drinking much more lowers blood sodium — hyponatremia: nausea, headache, confusion, seizures. The threshold can be changed in settings.
Tea, coffee, milk and soups count too. Log sugary drinks under Nutrition.

activity.serviceText: Tap to hide this notification. Counting continues.
activity.hideNotificationHint: Android requires a notification for background work. Switch off the “Step counting” channel — steps keep being counted.

stepsHintBaseline.$t: The first {0:n0} steps are already included in your everyday activity level, so calories are counted only above that.

info.title: How steps are counted
device: Steps are counted by the phone’s built-in step sensor — it runs all the time, even while Wellness is closed.

The app collects the count when you open it and roughly every 15–60 minutes in the background. If the system puts apps to sleep, the data simply arrives later — steps are not lost (except across a phone reboot).
On Xiaomi, Huawei, Honor and other phones with aggressive battery saving, enable autostart and “No restrictions” battery mode for Wellness, otherwise background updates may not run.
Wear a band or watch? Connect Health Connect and steps will come from there.
hc: Steps come from Health Connect: Google Fit, Mi Fitness, Zepp, Samsung Health and other apps write them there — even while Wellness is closed.
If steps don’t show up, check that the source app shares steps with Health Connect.
Until Health Connect is installed and connected, the phone’s sensor counts steps — nothing is lost.

activity.workoutsEmpty: Pick a template below or add your own workout
activity.templatesHint: Tap to log, long-press to edit.

estimate.$t: Estimate: {0:n0} kcal. If you have heart-rate monitor data, enter it instead.

activity.name: Name
activity.metHint: MET is how many times more energy an activity uses than rest. Light stretching ≈ 2.5, walking ≈ 3.5, strength training ≈ 5, running ≈ 8–11. Burn = (MET − 1) × weight × hours.

heart.how: Sit quietly for 5 minutes. No coffee, smoking or exercise for 30 minutes before. Back supported, legs uncrossed, cuff at heart level on a bare arm. Take 2 readings a minute apart and log the average.
heart.classNote: Per ACC/AHA 2017. Some countries use 140/90 as the hypertension threshold.
heart.urgent: Blood pressure above 180/120 with headache, chest pain, shortness of breath, speech or vision problems, or weakness in an arm/leg — call emergency services (112 / 911). The app does not diagnose.

crisis.label: Hypertensive crisis
crisis.advice: Measure again in 5 minutes. If it stays high or you have chest pain, shortness of breath, speech or vision problems — call emergency services.

stage2.label: Stage 2 hypertension
stage2.advice: Persistent values like this are a reason to see a doctor soon.

stage1.label: Stage 1 hypertension
stage1.advice: Discuss with your doctor. Less salt, more activity, healthy weight and sleep all help.

elevated.label: Elevated
elevated.advice: Not a disease yet, but a trend. Watch salt, weight and activity.

low.label: Low
low.advice: If you feel weak, dizzy or faint, see a doctor.

refWeight.$t: Protein and water targets use an adjusted weight of ≈ {0:n1} kg

body.why: People of the same weight can have very different body composition. Body fat and waist matter more: a waist-to-height ratio under 0.5 is a good sign, above 0.6 the risk of diabetes and heart disease rises sharply. With training, weight can stay flat while the waist shrinks.
body.measureNote: Fill in only what you measured.

navy.$t: Body fat estimate from measurements (US Navy method): {0:n1} %

body.weigh: In the morning, after the bathroom, before eating or drinking, in the same clothes. Weight fluctuates 1–2 kg with water and salt — watch the trend line.
body.trendNote: The bright line is the weighted average (exponential, each reading weighted by the time since the previous one, 7-day half-life). The green zone is a healthy BMI weight.

health.title: Health
health.empty: Keep doctor visits, lab tests and checkups here — with photos of reports and results.
health.removeText: Its photos will be deleted too.
health.privacy: Records and photos stay on the phone. Backups include the photos too.

pantry.title: Food at home
pantry.empty: Add what you have at home — the app will tell you what is about to spoil.
pantry.name: Name

baseHint.$t: Typical storage: {0} days. The date on the package wins.

pantry.source: Storage times: USDA FoodKeeper. Tags: UK FSA criteria and EU Regulation 1924/2006, per 100 g.

share.title: Shared pantry
share.about: Your pantry and shopping list sync between family phones through a shared code. Data is encrypted on the phone: the server stores only ciphertext and never sees the code. If nobody opens the shared list for 7 days, the cloud copy is deleted.
share.or: Or join with someone else's code:

joinText.$t: The shared list has {0} products, yours has {1}. Merge the lists or replace yours with the shared one?

share.yourCode: Shared list code. Give it to the people you want to share with:
share.leaveText: Products on this phone stay. Others can keep using the code.
share.expired: Sharing stopped: the cloud copy was deleted because nobody opened it for 7 days. Products on this phone are kept. Create a new code to share again.

errors.badCode: A code has 16 letters and digits, like ABCD-1234-EFGH-5678.
errors.notFound: Code not found, or the list has expired.
errors.network: Cannot reach the server. Check your connection.
errors.rateLimited: Too many requests. Try again later.
errors.full: The server is full. Try again later.
errors.tooBig: The list is too big to sync.
errors.corrupt: Could not decrypt the list. Check the code.

openedHint.$t: Keeps about {0} days once opened; the expiry date moves closer.

pantry.shopEmpty: The list is empty. Add what to buy, or use “Add to shopping list” on a finished product.
pantry.shopHint: Bought items show up on the “At home” page, where you can add them to the pantry.
pantry.statsEmpty: Statistics appear once you mark products as eaten or thrown away.
pantry.statsNote: Waste is the share thrown away: a product thrown away half-full counts as half. A product used up (0 %) counts as eaten.
pantry.boughtHint: Set the date and amount, or add as is with a date based on the product type.

finishedAsk.$t: Finished. Eaten or thrown away? Counts as eaten in {0} s.

pantry.historyEmpty: Products you eat or throw away will appear here.
pantry.historyHint: Tap an entry to fix or delete it.

settings.importText: Current data will be replaced with the file’s data. Continue?
settings.packHint: A file with a ready-made list of foods and their nutrition — say, the whole menu of your favourite café, or the meals from a plan your dietitian sent you. After importing, these foods show up in search and work offline. You can get such files from friends or the project community. Can't find something? Create it yourself (Add food → Create product, optionally based on a similar one) or look it up by barcode.

donation.evmNote: One address for all EVM networks. Double-check the network before sending: coins sent on the wrong network may be lost.

about.openSourceText: Wellness is free software under the GNU AGPL v3 license. No ads, accounts, analytics or trackers.
about.privacyText: All data stays on your device. The only network requests are the food search (Open Food Facts, USDA) and the GitHub update check, both optional. Reading steps from Health Connect is opt-in and stays on the phone.
sourcesList: Sugar, salt, potassium, trans fat: WHO guidelines
Protein, fat, carbs, fiber: US DRI (IOM), EFSA
Energy expenditure: Compendium of Physical Activities
Body fat: US Navy method (Hodgdon & Beckett)
Foods: Open Food Facts (ODbL), USDA FoodData Central, ANSES-CIQUAL 2020 (Etalab Open Licence), Skurikhin tables
about.importantText: Wellness is not a medical device and does not diagnose. All targets are general guidelines for healthy adults. With medical conditions, during pregnancy, for children and older adults they may differ — consult a doctor.
